steps.text: Gather all Ingredients. Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
Place sugar, eggs, and lemon juice in a blender; blend until smooth, about 3 minutes.
Pour melted butter into the blender and blend for 30 seconds more.
Transfer lemon filling to pastry shell.
Bake in the preheated oven until filling is just set, 30 to 35 minutes. Allow pie to rest until completely set before serving, about 15 minutes more.

raw_recipe.headline: Meyer Lemon Pie
raw_recipe.description: With only five ingredients and the help of a blender, you can have a silky, tangy Meyer lemon pie on your table in under an hour!
raw_recipe.name: Meyer Lemon Pie

review.reviewBody: I added a teaspoon of fresh lemon zest to the filling. After the pie had cooled, I spread Cool Whip over the top. I swear, I could eat a vat of this lemon pie filling. It's like a mixture of lemon curd and the filling from lemon meringue pie (which is the same thing, I guess). Delicious!

Taking in all reviews, thought I would put all tips together and see how it comes out. Very easy, beats using the stove method, loved it! Here it goes; I used a Trader Joe's pie crust. Pre-baked it for about 10 min & did egg wash and sprinkled some Turbinado sugar along the edges of crust for a little browning and crunch. I also preheated a flat baking sheet before placing pie pan on top to help cook bottom of crust. 
Used a tart pan, for visual effect. Sprayed it with oil. I find it browns the crust a little. The filling, used the Meyers lemons, I used an organic sugar, cut out 1/2 c. Will cut down a tad more next time I make it. I also added 3 tbs Red Mills Tapioca flour, for a little thickening, a pinch of salt, 1 tbs reg. lemon rind as well as Meyers. Followed the cooking directions. The only thing I didn't know if it was normal, my pie had little air holes all over top. Not sure if I cooked it too long or not enough or is that the norm. Anyone else experience this? My man loved it, he didn't think it was too sweet.

I made this recipe following a few suggestions from other bakers- Used 1 cup sugar, 1 capful vanilla extract, 5 eggs, 1/4 cup butter, zest and juice of a large Meyer lemon- Blend in vitamix for 3 minutes- I put my filling in individual custard cups and omitted the pie crust. Baked at 350 for 30 minutes- Turned out perfect- Will definitely make this again, as I too, have a dwarf Meyer lemon tree🍋

I loved this pie but I made a few changes. It seemed too sweet so I only used one cup sugar and then I used a whole cup of meyer lemon juice, because I like a tart flavor ( also I have a tree that is covered in Meyer lemons right now) then I thought it might be too runny so I used 5 eggs. I also added some lemon zest. I mixed it in blender and I was amazed how easy it was. I topped it off with a dollop if real whipped crème with more lemon zest The pie set up perfectly and was really delicious. My guests asked for seconds. I have to comment on the user who said it isn’t healthy. I think it’s much healthier than regular lemon meringue pie because I used less sugar and no cornstarch. Great recipe but with my modifications though it depends on your taste. You should taste the batter and adjust.

I used 1 cup of sugar, added zest, and 2tsp cornstarch. Also, I tore apart ready made pie crust and lined four ramekins for mini pies. I sprayed the ramekins with butter spray first and the pies released easily. Cooked about 30 minutes. Turned out perfect. Set nice and firm. Everything was great, but I think I will use the full amount of sugar next time. Definitely needs the whipped topping, too.

I used my own crust (1/2 shortening and 1/2 butter), and baked this in a standard Pyrex 9 inch pie pan. I increased all ingredients by 50%, using 4 large eggs. I added a tablespoon of lemon zest and 2 teaspoons of corn starch. The pie took about 40 minutes to cook. We topped it with whipped cream. Delicious!

After reading reviews, I used a store bought crust and pre-baked it for half the recommended time, then brushed the bottom with an egg white to the filling wouldn't make it soggy. Added 1 tsp of corn starch to the sugar mix. Very easy and quick and we loved it.

The other reviews were so helpful! I blind-baked the crust for twenty minutes on 350° and added the filling to a hot crust and continued baking at 325°. I added 1/2 tsp corn starch, reduced sugar to 1c, and used two whole eggs and one yolk (I only had XL eggs and I thought 3 whole eggs might add too much liquid to the filling). I would have shared a photo, but there isn't a crumb left! I will definitely be making this again since it only used 2 lemons from a 4lb bag!

This is a great recipe! I used 1/2 cup of key lime juice instead of lemon juice so it's a key lime pie rather than lemon pie. I also made my own pie crust with a different recipe instead of using a pastry shell (we may not have a pastry shell on hand). But anyways, it is a wonderful recipe. It's a lot of fun to make and eat!

I have also added lime juice & zest to the filling. I have made this recipe 4 times. The first time it came out perfect. I used my magic bullet to mix it. The next time I tried my stand mixer on high, hut it didn't get the fluff needed with the mixture (the egg component in the filling needs whipping fast & at least 3 minutes). The other times I have used a ninja mixer or immersion blender. 
It's a nice combination of sweet & tart!

This was so delicious and super easy to make. I followed the recipe exactly and my family loved it! I've made it a few times with some minor adjustments to thicken up the filling, I reduced the sugar to 1 cup, added both lemon and lime juice, and a 1/3 cup of shredded coconut. Disappears every time :)

I am guessing that bcuz I used Splenda instead of sugar, that's why it didn't set? Everything else was exactly the same! Why didn't it set?? Someone tell me. I LOVE LEMON PIE and want to make it again, but I am so unhappy! Fresh lemon juice, butter, eggs, sugar, pie crust wasted!
Loved it. I added about 1 ounce of Lemon extract to make it really lemony.
I bought a vegan pie shell, vegan butter, vegan sugar, vegan egg replacer
My husband has a Meyer Lemon Tree. This is our go to recipe when we have a glut of lemons. Add a dollop of whipped cream.

was gifted a box of Meyer lemons & found this recipe, couldn't be happier, easy to make & taste wonderful. used 4 oz of juice + some pulp & put in some of the zest both inside while blending & sprinkled some on top. Love that this isn't a sweet pie but with dusting of powdered sugar or any whipped topping it can be. Thanks for sharing, making some to give as gifts.
delish! like the description, tangy sweet and tart

I figured out why the pie filling poured like water - I wasn’t expecting ounces - therefore, against my better judgment at the time, added 3 3/4 cups of lemon juice. Made recipe again - turned out just fine.

This was easy to make and the recipe worked perfectly, though my filling browned a lot and didn't look like some of the pictures. I used Meyer Lemons as indicated. This is a very unhealthy pie, though! My family liked it, but we would prefer a different type, maybe less rich and made with flour.
We love this pie! Our Meyer's lemon tree is bountiful and I always have juice. So easy and we always have a can of whipped cream or scoop of vanilla ice cream in the frig to top it off.
